clue.text: Divide orange in two — such will be the aim

definitions.text: Divide orange in two — such will be the aim

parts.words: Divide orange in two — such will be the aim
parts.note: to split a small fruit with a shot you must fire from so close that there is no allowance for drop: the range at which you aim straight at the mark

explanation.surface: A marksman sets out to split an orange with a single shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot fired at a target so close that the sight needs no allowance is a shot at this range, aimed straight.

clue.text: Alexander meeting Joan at the card-table

definitions.text: Alexander meeting Joan at the card-table

parts.words: Alexander meeting Joan at the card-table
parts.note: the word that follows the poet's first name Alexander also prefixes Joan in the name of an old card game, and Alexander was a papal name

explanation.surface: A man named Alexander meets a woman named Joan over cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Catholic Church: the poet Alexander shares the title, as does the old game named after a legendary female pontiff.

clue.text: Where the duke ordered play to continue

definitions.text: Where the duke ordered play to continue

parts.words: Where the duke ordered play to continue
parts.note: Duke Orsino opens Twelfth Night with if music be the food of love, play on, in the land where the comedy is set

explanation.surface: A nobleman tells actors to keep performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic land where Shakespeare sets Twelfth Night, ruled by Duke Orsino.

clue.text: Moon lightens our darkness? Just the opposite on this occasion

definitions.text: Moon lightens our darkness? Just the opposite on this occasion

parts.words: Moon lightens our darkness? Just the opposite on this occasion
parts.note: the evening prayer asks lighten our darkness; when the moon wholly blocks the sun it darkens our light instead

explanation.surface: A prayer for the moon to light the night is turned on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon fully covers the sun, day goes dark: the complete obscuring of one body by another.

clue.text: Landlord's. strange silence on one point

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the landlord

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the second piece below the first
strange signals the word silence turned into an odd new order

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A landlord's eerie silence on a single point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges SILENCE to LICENSE; 'on' puts E below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub landlord holds the licence to sell alcohol.

clue.text: Sister embraces a religion, with fine distinction

indicators.note: embraces means the nun holds the next piece inside her

parts.note: a nun is called Sister
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nun takes up a faith with subtle discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, stands for a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle shade of meaning or difference.

clue.text: This is, that is could be, silicate

definitions.text: This is, that is could be, silicate

parts.words: This is, that is could be, silicate
parts.note: a riddle about minerals: this soft powdery one is a silicate, while another white stone may or may not be

explanation.surface: A pedantic mineralogist hedges over which stone is which compound.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle rather than a mechanism: the soft mineral used for baby powder really is a magnesium silicate.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft mineral ground into baby powder is hydrated magnesium silicate.

clue.text: Maladjusted one, right for old hospital job

annotationWithheld.why: Maladjusted one, right for old hospital job (7): ALMONER needs MAL from 'Maladjusted' as fodder while 'adjusted' in the same word is the anagram signal, so one printed word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Maladjusted one, right for old hospital job

clue.text: Doyle's professor going for the title?

definitions.meaning: Professor ... is Conan Doyle's hero of The Lost World
a boxer contesting a championship against the holder

explanation.surface: Conan Doyle's professor fancies a championship bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Doyle's Lost World scientist; also a contender seeking a holder's crown.

clue.text: He enjoys being crossed

parts.note: being crossed sounds like being thwarted, but on a ballot paper voters mark a cross beside the candidate they want, which pleases him

explanation.surface: Someone oddly delights in being thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: An election candidate is pleased when voters put their cross beside his name.

clue.text: She loved a man of high standing in London

definitions.text: She loved a man of high standing in London

parts.words: She loved a man of high standing in London
parts.note: the man of high standing is the admiral whose statue stands atop the column in Trafalgar Square; Lady Hamilton was his lover

explanation.surface: A woman fell for a socially prominent Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson stands on his column high above Trafalgar Square, so 'high standing' is literal; his mistress was Lady Hamilton.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Hamilton, Nelson's lover, had this first name.

clue.text: Friendly pose would get one poor dog nowhere

definitions.text: Friendly pose would get one poor dog nowhere

parts.words: Friendly pose would get one poor dog nowhere
parts.note: Old Mother Hubbard's dog fawned in vain because her larder was bare: affection feigned for the sake of food

explanation.surface: A dog's fawning wins it nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Hubbard is the nursery-rhyme woman who found her larder bare when she went to get her dog a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection shown only to get food or gain, like a pet fawning for a meal.

clue.text: Of mouth or ear, say

indicators.note: say asks the solver to hear the word for the ear spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the adjective for the ear is aural

explanation.surface: A doctor lists the body parts under examination: mouth or ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective for the ear, AURAL, sounds the same as the adjective for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective meaning relating to the mouth, as in spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Lord deliver us from such bumpers

definitions.text: Lord deliver us from such bumpers

parts.words: Lord deliver us from such bumpers
parts.note: the old Cornish prayer asks the Lord to deliver us from ghoulies, ghosties and things that go bump in the night

explanation.surface: Someone prays to be spared overfull glasses, bumpers being brimming drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A bumper is also a brimming glass, but here it is something that goes bump; the prayer places them at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go bump in the night are night-time creatures, active after dark.

clue.text: French paints, brushes, etc, adorning the mantelpiece ?

definitions.text: French paints, brushes, etc, adorning the mantelpiece ?

parts.words: French paints, brushes, etc, adorning the mantelpiece ?
parts.note: a French phrase that seems to mean art materials, though it denotes ornaments set on display

explanation.surface: Artists' supplies from France are left on the mantelpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for small decorative ornaments, literally things of art.

clue.text: Banking establishments note stock situations

parts.note: B is a musical note
ranches are places where livestock is kept

explanation.surface: Banks record the state of their shares.
explanation.definitionFit: Local offices of a bank are its outlets in different towns.

clue.text: Master of the 40-minute orbiter

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck boasts he will put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes; his master is the fairy king

explanation.surface: Someone controls a satellite with a forty-minute orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy king in Shakespeare's comedy is Puck's master.

clue.text: Hat Girl six furlongs ahead of Kipling Lady

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece above the next in a down answer

parts.note: a mile is eight furlongs, so six furlongs is three quarters of it: three of its four letters
Kipling's poem The Liner She's a Lady

explanation.surface: A girl in a race over six furlongs leads a filly named after Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: Three quarters of MILE (six of eight furlongs) gives MIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who makes and sells hats.

clue.text: Involve in a settlement

definitions.meaning: to necessitate or bring as a consequence
in law, a settlement of property restricting inheritance to a line of heirs

explanation.surface: Someone is drawn into a legal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve as a consequence; also a legal settlement fixing who inherits an estate.

clue.text: Can sea-bird find a place on the Wye?

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tern is a sea-bird

explanation.surface: Can a gull find somewhere to land on the river?
explanation.walkthrough: The Wye is a river on the England-Wales border; Tintern Abbey stands on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh village beside the Wye, famous for its ruined abbey.

clue.text: Primrose House ?

parts.note: Dr Primrose is the clergyman in Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield, so his house is the parson's residence

explanation.surface: The name of a house, perhaps a country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Primrose of Goldsmith's novel is a parish clergyman, whose home is the parsonage.

clue.text: Not without point in Africa, it's not quite gay enough for Paris

indicators.note: not quite means the French phrase falls one letter short

parts.note: French assez gai means gay enough

explanation.surface: Something in Africa is sharp, yet not quite cheerful enough for Parisians.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the Z of ASSEZ GAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples, which certainly has a point.

clue.text: A divine drink needed for Jonson's

definitions.text: A divine drink needed for Jonson's

parts.words: A divine drink needed for Jonson's
parts.note: in Ben Jonson's Song to Celia, the craving that from the soul doth rise doth ask a drink divine

explanation.surface: A heavenly beverage is required by the poet Jonson.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving for drink: in Jonson's song this longing asks a drink divine.

clue.text: Awkward scenes with Henry the steward

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of the word scenes are clumsily arranged

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A steward makes awkward scenes involving Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' is the anagram signal; Henry is shortened to the nickname Shakespeare gives the young Henry V, not the single letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was a medieval household official, an estate steward.

clue.text: Frustrate with a stroke of the pen

definitions.meaning: to ... hopes is to thwart them
a short horizontal line in writing

explanation.surface: Someone foils a plan with one stroke of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart hopes; also the short line written as punctuation.

clue.text: Unsaleable narcotic ?

definitions.meaning: a ... on the market is a product nobody will buy

explanation.surface: A narcotic that cannot be sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsellable goods are a glut on the market; also a medicine or narcotic.

clue.text: Monkey — sign …of …the "times"—makes summit

parts.note: an ape is a primate like a monkey
the multiplication sign, read as times, is X

explanation.surface: A monkey becomes a sign of the times by climbing to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' here is the multiplication sign, a wink at the newspaper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point, a peak or top.

clue.text: Early start in morning, or ruin for the tradesman

indicators.note: ruin tells us to wreck and rebuild the letters of the preceding words
the start of the word Early is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper faces an early start or ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' scrambles E (start of 'Early') with MORNING and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardware dealer is a shopkeeper selling tools and metal goods.

clue.text: Swimming backwards, a crazy sort of fish

indicators.note: swimming backwards tells us to read the words a crazy sort from the end

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A mad fish swims backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming backwards' turns A NUT round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean fish of the mackerel family, often canned.

clue.text: Robin the ill nourished tailor

definitions.meaning: Robin is the first name of the tailor among the rustic players in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A hungry tailor named Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is a name, not the bird: the tailor in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A starved, scrawny person; also the tailor in Shakespeare's mechanicals.
